culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Scottish Outdoor Access Code: there are statutory access rights to most land and water, used responsibly. Respect the interests of others (privacy, safety, livelihoods), care for the environment (wildlife, heritage, take litter home) and take responsibility for your own actions. Follow reasonable advice from land managers.
culture-and-protocol.note: From the Scottish Government's own agency.

laws.rule: The Visitor Levy (Scotland) Act 2024 lets Scottish councils charge a levy on paid overnight stays. Edinburgh's levy, the first, is 5% of the accommodation cost for up to five consecutive nights, for stays from 24 July 2026 booked or paid on or after 1 October 2025, collected by the accommodation provider.

laws.rule: Scotland's drink-drive limit is lower than the rest of the UK: 50 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood (22 micrograms per 100 ml of breath).

laws.rule: Maeshowe Chambered Cairn is entered by guided tour only, starting at the Stenness visitor centre.

Loch Lomond and the Trossachs National Park: byelaws on camping and fires apply in the Camping Management Zones from March to September. In that season camping there needs a campsite booking or a permit. Outside the zones the park says wild camping is still possible under the Scottish Outdoor Access Code. The park asks campers to take litter home, to go to the toilet at least 30 metres from open water, people or buildings, and, if they plan a fire, to bring firewood and a firepit and not cut trees or move dead wood. The page names no fine.

Cairngorms National Park: from 1 April to 30 September each year, fires and barbecues are banned across the park under a fire management byelaw. The park says breaking it could bring a fine of up to GBP 500 (about A$951, RBA 30 Oct 2026). Outside those dates the park asks visitors not to light a fire anywhere, and notes the Scottish Outdoor Access Code says never to light one in woods, on peaty ground, farmland, near buildings or at high fire risk. Wild camping is permitted if done responsibly: small numbers and two or three nights at most in one place.

layers.authority: Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park Authority
layers.process: Camping Management Zones, made by byelaws in 2017, cover busy lochshores from 1 March to 30 September. In that season you book a campsite, or a permit for a permit area, to camp, or in some areas to stay overnight in a campervan. A permit costs GBP 4.50 per tent or vehicle per night (about A$8.56, RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = GBP 0.5258), for up to three nights in one area, booked up to four weeks ahead. It covers any spot inside the permit area, with no set pitch and no facilities. Tents: arrive from 1pm, leave by 11am. Campervans: the permit runs 7pm to 10am. From 1 October to 28 February no permit is needed. The Authority is reviewing the byelaws, with a public consultation planned for July to September 2026.

layers.authority: Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park Authority
layers.process: The Authority's own campsites at Loch Chon, Loch Achray, Inchcailloch and Sallochy are closed from 1 October 2026 to 28 February 2027. Outside the Camping Management Zones, wild camping follows the Scottish Outdoor Access Code.
